ESV.1: In the days when the judges ruled there was a famine in the land, and a man of Bethlehem in Judah went to sojourn in the country of Moab, he and his wife and his two sons.
ESV.2: The name of the man was Elimelech and the name of his wife Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They went into the country of Moab and remained there.
ESV.3: But Elimelech, the husband of Naomi, died, and she was left with her two sons.
ESV.4: These took Moabite wives; the name of the one was Orpah and the name of the other Ruth. They lived there about ten years,
ESV.5: and both Mahlon and Chilion died, so that the woman was left without her two sons and her husband.
ESV.6: Then she arose with her daughters-in-law to return from the country of Moab, for she had heard in the fields of Moab that the LORD had visited his people and given them food.
ESV.7: So she set out from the place where she was with her two daughters-in-law, and they went on the way to return to the land of Judah.
ESV.8: But Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go, return each of you to her mother's house. May the LORD deal kindly with you, as you have dealt with the dead and with me.
ESV.9: The LORD grant that you may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband!” Then she kissed them, and they lifted up their voices and wept.
ESV.10: And they said to her, “No, we will return with you to your people.”
ESV.11: But Naomi said, “Turn back, my daughters; why will you go with me? Have I yet sons in my womb that they may become your husbands?
ESV.12: Turn back, my daughters; go your way, for I am too old to have a husband. If I should say I have hope, even if I should have a husband this night and should bear sons,
ESV.13: would you therefore wait till they were grown? Would you therefore refrain from marrying? No, my daughters, for it is exceedingly bitter to me for your sake that the hand of the LORD has gone out against me.”
ESV.14: Then they lifted up their voices and wept again. And Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.
ESV.15: And she said, “See, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her gods; return after your sister-in-law.”
ESV.16: But Ruth said, “Do not urge me to leave you or to return from following you. For where you go I will go, and where you lodge I will lodge. Your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
ESV.17: Where you die I will die, and there will I be buried. May the LORD do so to me and more also if anything but death parts me from you.”
ESV.18: And when Naomi saw that she was determined to go with her, she said no more.
ESV.19: So the two of them went on until they came to Bethlehem. And when they came to Bethlehem, the whole town was stirred because of them. And the women said, “Is this Naomi?”
ESV.20: She said to them, “Do not call me Naomi;  call me Mara,  for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
ESV.21: I went away full, and the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi, when the LORD has testified against me and the Almighty has brought calamity upon me?”
ESV.22: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabite her daughter-in-law with her, who returned from the country of Moab. And they came to Bethlehem at the beginning of barley harvest.

NKJV.1: Now it came to pass, in the days when the judges ruled, that there was a famine in the land. And a certain man of Bethlehem, Judah, went to dwell in the country of Moab, he and his wife and his two sons.
NKJV.2: The name of the man was Elimelech, the name of his wife was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion— Ephrathites of Bethlehem, Judah. And they went to the country of Moab and remained there.
NKJV.3: Then Elimelech, Naomi’s husband, died; and she was left, and her two sons.
NKJV.4: Now they took wives of the women of Moab: the name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other Ruth. And they dwelt there about ten years.
NKJV.5: Then both Mahlon and Chilion also died; so the woman survived her two sons and her husband.
NKJV.6: Then she arose with her daughters-in-law that she might return from the country of Moab, for she had heard in the country of Moab that the LORD had visited His people by giving them bread.
NKJV.7: Therefore she went out from the place where she was, and her two daughters-in-law with her; and they went on the way to return to the land of Judah.
NKJV.8: And Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go, return each to her mother’s house. The LORD deal kindly with you, as you have dealt with the dead and with me.
NKJV.9: The LORD grant that you may find rest, each in the house of her husband.” So she kissed them, and they lifted up their voices and wept.
NKJV.10: And they said to her, “Surely we will return with you to your people.”
NKJV.11: But Naomi said, “Turn back, my daughters; why will you go with me? Are there still sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands?
NKJV.12: Turn back, my daughters, go—for I am too old to have a husband. If I should say I have hope, if I should have a husband tonight and should also bear sons,
NKJV.13: would you wait for them till they were grown? Would you restrain yourselves from having husbands? No, my daughters; for it grieves me very much for your sakes that the hand of the LORD has gone out against me!”
NKJV.14: Then they lifted up their voices and wept again; and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.
NKJV.15: And she said, “Look, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her gods; return after your sister-in-law.”
NKJV.16: But Ruth said: “Entreat me not to leave you, Or to turn back from following after you; For wherever you go, I will go; And wherever you lodge, I will lodge; Your people shall be my people, And your God, my God.
NKJV.17: Where you die, I will die, And there will I be buried. The LORD do so to me, and more also, If anything but death parts you and me.”
NKJV.18: When she saw that she was determined to go with her, she stopped speaking to her.
NKJV.19: Now the two of them went until they came to Bethlehem. And it happened, when they had come to Bethlehem, that all the city was excited because of them; and the women said, “Is this Naomi?”
NKJV.20: But she said to them, “Do not call me Naomi; call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
NKJV.21: I went out full, and the LORD has brought me home again empty. Why do you call me Naomi, since the LORD has testified against me, and the Almighty has afflicted me?”
NKJV.22: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess her daughter-in-law with her, who returned from the country of Moab. Now they came to Bethlehem at the beginning of barley harvest.

WEB.1: In the days when the judges judged, there was a famine in the land. A certain man of Bethlehem Judah went to live in the country of Moab, he, and his wife, and his two sons.
WEB.2: The name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi. The names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Bethlehem Judah. They came into the country of Moab, and lived there.
WEB.3: Elimelech, Naomi’s husband, died; and she was left with her two sons.
WEB.4: They took for themselves wives of the women of Moab. The name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other was Ruth. They lived there about ten years.
WEB.5: Mahlon and Chilion both died, and the woman was bereaved of her two children and of her husband.
WEB.6: Then she arose with her daughters-in-law, that she might return from the country of Moab; for she had heard in the country of Moab how Yahweh  had visited his people in giving them bread.
WEB.7: She went out of the place where she was, and her two daughters-in-law with her. They went on the way to return to the land of Judah.
WEB.8: Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go, return each of you to her mother’s house. May Yahweh deal kindly with you, as you have dealt with the dead, and with me.
WEB.9: May Yahweh grant you that you may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband.” Then she kissed them, and they lifted up their voices, and wept.
WEB.10: They said to her, “No, but we will return with you to your people.”
WEB.11: Naomi said, “Go back, my daughters. Why do you want to go with me? Do I still have sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands?
WEB.12: Go back, my daughters, go your way; for I am too old to have a husband. If I should say, ‘I have hope,’ if I should even have a husband tonight, and should also bear sons;
WEB.13: would you then wait until they were grown? Would you then refrain from having husbands? No, my daughters, for it grieves me seriously for your sakes, for Yahweh’s hand has gone out against me.”
WEB.14: They lifted up their voices, and wept again; then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth joined with her.
WEB.15: She said, “Behold,  your sister-in-law has gone back to her people, and to her god. Follow your sister-in-law.”
WEB.16: Ruth said, “Don’t urge me to leave you, and to return from following you, for where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God  my God.
WEB.17: Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May Yahweh do so to me, and more also, if anything but death parts you and me.”
WEB.18: When she saw that she was determined to go with her, she stopped urging her.
WEB.19: So they both went until they came to Bethlehem. When they had come to Bethlehem, all the city was excited about them, and they asked, “Is this Naomi?”
WEB.20: She said to them, “Don’t call me Naomi.  Call me Mara;  for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
WEB.21: I went out full, and Yahweh has brought me home again empty. Why do you call me Naomi, since Yahweh has testified against me, and the Almighty has afflicted me?”
WEB.22: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, with her, who returned out of the country of Moab. They came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.

CSB17.1: During the time <sup>[1]</sup> of the judges, <sup>ⓖ</sup> there was a famine in the land. <sup>ⓗ</sup> A man left Bethlehem <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓘ</sup> in Judah with his wife and two sons to stay in the territory of Moab for a while.
CSB17.2: The man’s name was Elimelech, <sup>[3]</sup> and his wife’s name was Naomi. <sup>[4]</sup> The names of his two sons were Mahlon <sup>[5]</sup> and Chilion. <sup>[6]</sup> They were Ephrathites <sup>ⓙ</sup> from Bethlehem in Judah. They entered the fields of Moab and settled there.
CSB17.3: Naomi’s husband Elimelech died, and she was left with her two sons.
CSB17.4: Her sons took Moabite women as their wives: one was named Orpah and the second was named Ruth. After they lived in Moab about ten years,
CSB17.5: both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and Naomi was left without her two children and without her husband.
CSB17.6: She and her daughters-in-law set out to return from the territory of Moab, because she had heard in Moab that the LORD had paid attention to his people’s need by providing them food. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.7: She left the place where she had been living, accompanied by her two daughters-in-law, and traveled along the road leading back to the land of Judah.
CSB17.8: Naomi said to them, “Each of you go back to your mother’s home. <sup>ⓛ</sup> May the LORD show kindness to you as you have shown to the dead and to me.
CSB17.9: May the LORD grant each of you rest <sup>ⓜ</sup> in the house of a new husband.” She kissed them, and they wept loudly.
CSB17.10: They said to her, “We insist on returning with you to your people.”
CSB17.11: But Naomi replied, “Return home, my daughters. Why do you want to go with me? Am I able to have any more sons who could become your husbands? <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.12: Return home, my daughters. Go on, for I am too old to have another husband. Even if I thought there was still hope for me to have a husband tonight and to bear sons,
CSB17.13: would you be willing to wait for them to grow up? Would you restrain yourselves from remarrying? <sup>[7]</sup> No, my daughters, my life is much too bitter for you to share, <sup>[8]</sup> because the LORD’s hand has turned against me.” <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.14: Again they wept loudly, and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.
CSB17.15: Naomi said, “Look, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her gods. <sup>ⓑ</sup> Follow your sister-in-law.”
CSB17.16:
But Ruth replied: Don’t plead with me to abandon you
or to return and not follow you.
For wherever you go, I will go,
and wherever you live, I will live;
your people will be my people,
and your God will be my God.
CSB17.17:
Where you die, I will die,
and there I will be buried.
May the LORD punish me, [9] ⓒ
and do so severely,
if anything but death separates you and me.
CSB17.18: When Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped talking to her.
CSB17.19: The two of them traveled until they came to Bethlehem. When they entered Bethlehem, the whole town was excited about their arrival <sup>[10]</sup> <sup>ⓓ</sup> and the local women exclaimed, “Can this be Naomi?”
CSB17.20: “Don’t call me Naomi. Call me Mara,” <sup>[11]</sup> she answered, “for the Almighty <sup>ⓔ</sup> has made me very bitter. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.21: I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. <sup>ⓖ</sup> Why do you call me Naomi, since the LORD has opposed <sup>[12]</sup> me, and the Almighty has afflicted me?”
CSB17.22: So Naomi came back from the territory of Moab with her daughter-in-law Ruth the Moabitess. They arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest. <sup>ⓗ</sup>

NLT.1: In the days when the judges ruled in Israel, a severe famine came upon the land. So a man from Bethlehem in Judah left his home and went to live in the country of Moab, taking his wife and two sons with him.
NLT.2: The man’s name was Elimelech, and his wife was Naomi. Their two sons were Mahlon and Kilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in the land of Judah. And when they reached Moab, they settled there.
NLT.3: Then Elimelech died, and Naomi was left with her two sons.
NLT.4: The two sons married Moabite women. One married a woman named Orpah, and the other a woman named Ruth. But about ten years later,
NLT.5: both Mahlon and Kilion died. This left Naomi alone, without her two sons or her husband.
NLT.6: Then Naomi heard in Moab that the LORD had blessed his people in Judah by giving them good crops again. So Naomi and her daughters-in-law got ready to leave Moab to return to her homeland.

AMP.1: In the days when the judges governed [Israel], there was a famine in the land [of Canaan]. And a certain man of Bethlehem in Judah went to live temporarily in the country of Moab with his wife and his two sons.

AMP.3: Then Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left [a widow] with her two sons.
AMP.4: They took wives from the Moabite women; the name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other was Ruth. They lived there about ten years;
AMP.5: and then both Mahlon and Chilion also died, so the woman [Naomi] was left without her two sons and her husband.
AMP.6: Then she set out with her daughters-in-law to return from the country of Moab, for she had heard in Moab how the LORD had taken care of His people [of Judah] in giving them food.

AMP.13: would you wait until they were grown? Would you go without marrying? No, my daughters; for it is much more difficult for me than for you, because the <e>Lord's</e> hand has gone against me."
AMP.14: Then they wept aloud again; and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law [goodbye], but Ruth clung to her.
AMP.15: Then Naomi said, "Look, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her gods; turn back and follow your sister-in-law."

NET.1: During the time of the judges there was a famine in the land of Judah. So a man from Bethlehem in Judah went to live as a resident foreigner in the region of Moab, along with his wife and two sons.
NET.2: (Now the man’s name was Elimelech, his wife was Naomi, and his two sons were Mahlon and Kilion. They were of the clan of Ephrath from Bethlehem in Judah.) They entered the region of Moab and settled there.
NET.3: Sometime later Naomi’s husband Elimelech died, so she and her two sons were left alone.
NET.4: So her sons married Moabite women. (One was named Orpah and the other Ruth.) And they continued to live there about ten years.
NET.5: Then Naomi’s two sons, Mahlon and Kilion, also died. So the woman was left all alone — bereaved of her two children as well as her husband!
NET.6: So she decided to return home from the region of Moab, accompanied by her daughters-in-law, because while she was living in Moab she had heard that the LORD had shown concern for his people, reversing the famine by providing abundant crops.
NET.7: Now as she and her two daughters-in-law began to leave the place where she had been living to return to the land of Judah,
NET.8: Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Listen to me! Each of you should return to your mother’s home! May the LORD show you the same kind of devotion that you have shown to your deceased husbands and to me!
NET.9: May the LORD enable each of you to find security in the home of a new husband!” Then she kissed them goodbye and they wept loudly.
NET.10: But they said to her, “No! We will return with you to your people.”
NET.11: But Naomi replied, “Go back home, my daughters! There is no reason for you to return to Judah with me! I am no longer capable of giving birth to sons who might become your husbands!
NET.12: Go back home, my daughters! For I am too old to get married again. Even if I thought that there was hope that I could get married tonight and conceive sons,
NET.13: surely you would not want to wait until they were old enough to marry! Surely you would not remain unmarried all that time! No, my daughters, you must not return with me. For my intense suffering is too much for you to bear. For the LORD is afflicting me!”
NET.14: Again they wept loudly. Then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung tightly to her.
NET.15: So Naomi said, “Look, your sister-in-law is returning to her people and to her god. Follow your sister-in-law back home!”
NET.16: But Ruth replied, “Stop urging me to abandon you! For wherever you go, I will go. Wherever you live, I will live. Your people will become my people, and your God will become my God.
NET.17: Wherever you die, I will die — and there I will be buried. May the LORD punish me severely if I do not keep my promise! Only death will be able to separate me from you!”
NET.18: When Naomi realized that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped trying to dissuade her.
NET.19: So the two of them journeyed together until they arrived in Bethlehem. When they entered Bethlehem, the whole village was excited about their arrival. The women of the village said, “Can this be Naomi?”
NET.20: But she replied to them, “Don’t call me ‘Naomi’! Call me ‘Mara’ because the Sovereign One has treated me very harshly.
NET.21: I left here full, but the LORD has caused me to return empty-handed. Why do you call me ‘Naomi,’ seeing that the LORD has opposed me, and the Sovereign One has caused me to suffer?”
NET.22: So Naomi returned, accompanied by her Moabite daughter-in-law Ruth, who came back with her from the region of Moab. (Now they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.)
